back: Mass × velocity, p = mv: a vector, in kg m s⁻¹ (N s).
The resultant force equals the rate of change of momentum, in the direction of the change.
Force × time for which it acts; equal to the change in momentum and to the area under a force-time graph.

front: How does F = ma follow from F = Δp/Δt?
back: For constant mass, $\Delta(mv)/\Delta t = m\,\Delta v/\Delta t = ma$.

front: Why do crumple zones, airbags and seat belts work?
back: They increase the stopping time for the same change in momentum, so the force is smaller.

front: Force from a jet that stops at a wall
back: $F = \dfrac{\Delta m}{\Delta t}v$ (doubled if the jet bounces straight back at the same speed)

front: Change in momentum of a rebounding ball
back: $m(v + u)$ in size (speeds), directed along the rebound: the momenta add because the direction reverses.
